payload.purpose_context: Phase 4a delivered the visual vocabulary, primitives, and a browsable gallery. This mission finishes Phase 4 by adding the configurable controls and reusable compositions that later screens compose from, wiring the production shell to use them, and extending the gallery demo scene so every control and composition can be seen and judged by eye. No MIDI or audio is involved.
payload.purpose_tldr: Build the reusable controls and compositions the real screens get assembled from, and a demo scene that shows them all.

payload.wp_title: Component family scaffold and the total selector
Content compositions and the no-placeholder rule
Gallery pages, stepping, and measured silence
Deterministic proof and the DESIGN/ROADMAP corrections

The footer click-count decision was right on the merits and is now justified correctly: the shipped paint_footer already emitted from ui.add(button).clicked() with a keyline and a MIN_INTERACTIVE_TARGET_PX floor, so the targets preserve shipped behaviour and a Steam Deck touch target; the false 'clicks>=8' justification is gone and the Figma divergence stays recorded as raised-not-resolved.

review.reason: ARBITER DECISION after 3 review cycles (implement-review Step 5, Option A). OVERRIDE RATIONALE: the blocking artifact review-cycle-4.md is not a cycle-4 review - no cycle-4 review exists, because cycle 4 was orchestrator-directed with no reviewer. The file is the cycle-3 rejection wrapped in a stale header: double frontmatter, cycle_number 4 / verdict rejected wrapping cycle_number 3 with the cycle-3 reviewed_at and affected_files. Inspected before overriding. This is the same artifact-numbering defect recorded as waiver W-01 in cross-wp-findings.md, now its third occurrence. WHY CYCLE 4 EXISTED: the cycle-3 reviewer approved WP04 and then withdrew its own approval when three later lenses returned two defects it had missed, both reproduced. Its misses are recorded: it ran targeted filters (--lib compositions::footer) instead of the whole module so it never saw defect A fire, and it audited a reapplied file at item granularity - every const, function, test, doc heading present - while the loss was inside a surviving test body. Cycle 4 was scope-locked to exactly those two defects; the implementer honored the bound (2 owned files, 72 insertions / 10 deletions, no production code touched, all seven record-and-route items left alone). ORCHESTRATOR VERIFIED INDEPENDENTLY, not accepted on report: cargo fmt 0, clippy --all-targets -D warnings 0, cargo test 816 passed / 0 failed / 1 ignored. Fix A: the invented-text rule iterates the three bands WP04 fills via band_runs, matching its band-scoped siblings, with a per-band non-vacuity guard; whitelist unchanged, not widened. Reproduced both directions against a WP05 stand-in - 56/0/1 with the fix, and 55 passed / 1 failed reverting only the loop, emitting the reviewer's exact message. The failing run proves the stand-in genuinely paints, so the pass is the fix and not a no-op stand-in. Fix B: T019's invariant restored geometrically - the mark must sit nearer the active label than the inactive one, measured off band_runs - replacing cycle 2's assert!(marked[0].contains(active.label())) which splitting the mark into its own run made inexpressible. Mutation-verified: flipping context == active to context != active fails with 'the mark sits 60 px from PATCH and 8 px from MIXER, so it marks the inactive entry'. Restored from a file backup, not git checkout. CARRIED FORWARD, recorded not latent: the reachability sweep's band_rects aim fallback is a false-negative trap whose intuitive repair would gut the test - WP08 inherits it with T044; the footer reserve is 3.75 percent of the band against the shipped 38 percent; live_demo_runner.rs remains unowned. Approved rather than escalated because both defects were real, reproduced, fixed, and independently re-verified.

Review passed (cycle 2). ARTIFACT OVERRIDE, W-01 fifth occurrence: approval was refused with 'WP09 has a rejected review artifact (review-cycle-2.md)'. I INSPECTED THE BLOCKING FILE. It is a copy of my own cycle-1 rejection, not a second one - stripping frontmatter, its body is byte-identical to review-cycle-1.md (17,285 bytes each) and opens '# WP09 review - cycle 1'. Only its frontmatter differs, carrying cycle_number 2 and an inherited verdict rejected, written by move-task when I rejected cycle 1. There is exactly one WP09 rejection and it is cycle 1; there is no cycle-3 artifact. This is the documented artifact-numbering defect, now confirmed to fire on a WP's FIRST rejection. Per W-01 this is a process/tooling gate, self-service waivable with in-repo rationale; it is not a product or proof gate. Recorded in cross-wp-findings.

82/86 MEASUREMENT CONFIRMED against the live design file in cycle 1, unchanged since: Figma 42:25 holds sixteen Fader/Txx at width 82, x = 0,86...1290 (pitch 86), inside 42:20's 1452 px content; 15x86+82 = 1372 <= 1452. MIXER_TRACK_MIN_WIDTH_PX = 176.0 is 2.15x the authored 82 and 16x176 = 2816 > 1500, the only reason ScrollArea::horizontal exists at eframe_graphical_window.rs:512 - WP06 can retire it; it was compensating for an invented constant, not carrying load.

T048 OVERRUN RULING (cycle 1, reaffirmed): ACCEPTED. The bound was unsatisfiable as written - stripping the attributes fails the declared gate with 'constant STRIP_COLUMN_COUNT is never used' at exit 101, and deleting the constant would have required editing a WP03 test that reads it three times, which NFR-005 forbids. Asking for the ruling rather than deciding was correct.

ALL FOUR CYCLE-1 SURVIVORS NOW DIE BY NAME - re-applied by me against 384e71e, not taken on report: bank divides the content rect itself at 90.75 -> sixteen_columns_seat_inside_the_main_surface_at_both_viewports ('Desktop painted column 0 86.75 px wide against the declared 82'); literal 0 in every empty column -> a_marked_bank_paints_exactly_its_structure_names_and_nothing_else, now exact ordered equality rather than substring explainability; paint_separators a no-op AND hairlines moved onto the column edge -> both fifteen_hairlines_sit_on_the_gutter_midpoints_at_both_viewports; all cells collapsed onto one y -> a_column_cells_stack_down_it_without_overlapping_at_both_viewports. The pin is real and bidirectional: extents are still measured from the paint and now also pinned to mixer_column(), with density.rs pinning that to the 82-on-86 measured grid.

THREE JUDGEMENTS. (1) The ROWS -> ROW production edit is ACCEPTED: the crest-spec is genuinely singular (shell.yaml:271 'marks that row unavailable inside its own column'); it is a label's name and value with no logic; the constant is read only inside its own file; and it closes a real defect I flagged in cycle 1 that could not be closed test-only without asserting a known-broken layout or making a far larger geometry change. It is guarded - reverting to the plural fails the_marked_column_never_collides_its_name_with_its_mark at exactly 0.71875 px, matching my independent cycle-1 measurement. (2) Declining probe::Painted's shape count is ACCEPTED and is BETTER than what I proposed: my own moved-hairline mutation keeps the count at fifteen, so only the position assertion catches it; section.rs left untouched as instructed. (3) Declining both fader.rs items is ACCEPTED as compliance with a scope-locked cycle, and the argument checks out - column_pitch_px is called only by column_width_px, so reading .width_px directly would make it production-dead and need another suppression.

BOTH CORRECTIONS VERIFIED, not assumed: the second cfg(test) was a cascade its own remedy created; and column_rect's placement is byte-unchanged between cycles, so the geometry was always right and only the note was wrong - SteamDeck column 15 is [856, 908] against a 944 content edge, so 856 was a left edge reported where Desktop reported a right edge.

GATES RUN BY ME on the whole module, exit codes captured, no pipes: fmt 0, clippy --all-targets -D warnings 0 with zero warnings, cargo test 0, 814 passed / 0 failed. Baseline 796 (measured by me in an isolated worktree) -> 814 = +18; growth from +14 accounted for exactly by 3 new mixer_strip_bank tests and 1 new density test.
